episodes.title: Why the Monsoon Comes
sources: IMD: normal onset over Kerala 1 June; covers the country by 8 July (normal dates revised 2020)
IMD: June–September brings about 75% of India's annual rainfall
NCERT Class 11, Fundamentals of Physical Geography / India Physical Environment, chapter on climate

quiz.q: What starts the south-west monsoon's inflow?
options: The sea heats faster than the land
The land heats faster than the sea, lowering pressure over it
quiz.why: Hot air over the land rises, pressure falls, and cooler wet sea air is pulled in.

quiz.q: When does the monsoon normally reach Kerala?
quiz.why: IMD's normal onset over Kerala is 1 June; it covers the country by about 8 July.

quiz.q: About how much of India's yearly rain falls from June to September?
quiz.why: June to September brings about 75% of the year's rain.

review.note: Facts were read against IMD's normal onset and rainfall pages and the NCERT climate chapter. Diagrams are schematic, with no map. Moving facts: IMD's normal onset dates were revised in 2020 and may be revised again.

episodes.title: Chandrayaan-3 in 60 Seconds
sources: ISRO Chandrayaan-3 mission page and press releases, Jul–Sep 2023: launch 14 Jul 2023 (LVM3-M4), landing 23 Aug 2023, rover traverse ~100 m, LIBS confirmed sulphur, Vikram hop 3 Sep 2023 (~40 cm)
PIB, 26 Aug 2023: landing site named Shiv Shakti point; 23 August declared National Space Day

quiz.q: On which date did Vikram land near the Moon's south pole?
quiz.why: Launch was 14 July; the landing came on 23 August 2023, now National Space Day.

quiz.q: Why does the lunar south pole interest scientists?
options: It is the Moon's hottest spot
Some craters never see sunlight and may hold water ice
It faces the Earth all the time
It has the Moon's tallest mountain
quiz.why: Permanently shadowed craters may hold water ice.

quiz.q: What is the landing site called?
quiz.why: The landing spot was named Shiv Shakti point (PIB, 26 August 2023).

review.note: Facts were read against ISRO's Chandrayaan-3 mission pages and PIB releases (Jul–Sep 2023). Footage is ISRO's, under GODL-India. Moving facts: none known.

episodes.title: The Case That Limits Parliament
sources: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala, (1973) 4 SCC 225, decided 24 April 1973; 13-judge bench, 7:6
Hearing of 68 days (31 Oct 1972 – 23 Mar 1973), per Supreme Court of India records and standard texts (M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity)
Basic structure elements named in later cases: Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975), Minerva Mills (1980), S.R. Bommai (1994)

quiz.q: Under which Article can Parliament amend the Constitution?
quiz.why: Article 368 gives Parliament the power to amend.

quiz.q: How was Kesavananda Bharati decided?
quiz.why: Thirteen judges, the largest bench ever, split seven to six.

quiz.q: What did the court hold?
options: Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights at all
Parliament can amend any part, but not destroy the basic structure
Only states can amend the Constitution
quiz.why: Any part may be amended, but the basic structure must stand.

review.note: Facts were read against the Kesavananda Bharati judgment ((1973) 4 SCC 225) and a standard polity text. Retold lines: none. Moving facts: none known.

episodes.title: El Niño and India's Rain
sources: NCERT Class 11, India: Physical Environment, ch. 4 (Climate): El Niño, warm current off Peru, linked to weaker Indian monsoon; used in long-range forecasts
NOAA Climate.gov, 'What is the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) in a nutshell?': trade winds weaken in El Niño, warm water shifts east; La Niña is the cool phase; episodes recur every 2–7 years
IMD, Monsoon Report 1997: all-India June–September rainfall was 102% of the long-period average despite a strong El Niño; positive Indian Ocean Dipole cited

quiz.q: What happens to the Pacific trade winds in an El Niño year?
quiz.why: Weaker trade winds let the warm water spread east.

quiz.q: Why does El Niño often weaken India's monsoon?
options: It cools the Bay of Bengal
More air sinks over India instead of rising
quiz.why: With the rising air shifted east, more air sinks over India, so less rain.

quiz.q: What does 1997 show?
options: A strong El Niño can still come with a normal monsoon
La Niña causes floods every year
quiz.why: 1997 had a very strong El Niño but a normal monsoon.

review.note: Facts were read against NCERT's climate chapter, NOAA's ENSO explainer and IMD's 1997 monsoon figures. Diagrams are schematic, no map. Moving facts: none; the El Niño–monsoon link is a tendency, stated as one.

episodes.title: How a Cyclone Is Born
sources: NCERT Class 11, Fundamentals of Physical Geography, ch. 10 (Atmospheric Circulation and Weather Systems): conditions for tropical cyclones (sea surface above 27°C, Coriolis force, small vertical wind shear, pre-existing low-pressure disturbance); energy from latent heat of condensation; dissipate over land; the eye
IMD, Frequently Asked Questions on Tropical Cyclones: Bay of Bengal sees about four times as many cyclones as the Arabian Sea; peaks in April–May and October–December

quiz.q: Where does a tropical cyclone get its energy?
options: From heat released when water vapour condenses
quiz.why: Rising moist air condenses into cloud and releases latent heat.

quiz.q: Why don't cyclones form right on the equator?
options: The Earth's spin (Coriolis force) is too weak there to twist the air
quiz.why: Without the Coriolis force, the inflowing air doesn't spiral.

quiz.q: Which sea sees more cyclones?
options: Bay of Bengal, about four to one
quiz.why: IMD gives roughly four Bay of Bengal cyclones for each Arabian Sea one.

review.note: Facts were read against NCERT's chapter on weather systems and IMD's cyclone FAQ. Satellite photos are from the ISS, over open ocean, with no lines drawn. Moving facts: the four-to-one ratio is a long-term average; recent decades show more Arabian Sea cyclones.

episodes.title: Western Disturbances: Winter Rain in the North
sources: NCERT Class 11, India: Physical Environment, ch. 4 (Climate): western cyclonic disturbances originate over the Mediterranean Sea, are brought into India by the westerly jet stream, cause winter rainfall in the north-western plains, which is beneficial for rabi crops; snowfall in the Himalayas
IMD Glossary, 'Western Disturbance': an extra-tropical storm from the Mediterranean region bringing winter rain to north-west India

quiz.q: Where do western disturbances form?
quiz.why: They begin over the Mediterranean region and travel east.

quiz.q: What carries them to India?
options: Westerly winds high in the sky
quiz.why: The westerly jet stream carries them east.

quiz.q: Which crop benefits most from their rain?
quiz.why: Winter rain in the north-west waters the rabi crop.

review.note: Facts were read against NCERT's climate chapter and the IMD glossary. Snow pictures are from Nepal and Gulmarg; no map. Moving facts: none.

episodes.title: How a Delta Grows
sources: NCERT Class 11, Fundamentals of Physical Geography, ch. 7 (Landforms and their Evolution): deltas form where rivers deposit their load at the mouth; coarser material settles first; distributaries

NCERT Class 11, India: Physical Environment, ch. 3 (Drainage System): Ganga–Brahmaputra delta is the world's largest; Narmada and Tapi flow west through rift valleys and form estuaries; east-flowing peninsular rivers form deltas
UNESCO World Heritage List, The Sundarbans (Bangladesh) and Sundarbans National Park (India): largest mangrove forest in the world

quiz.q: Why does a river drop its silt at the sea?
options: The sea pushes it back up
quiz.why: A slower river can't carry its load, so the silt settles.

quiz.q: What are distributaries?
options: Smaller channels a river splits into near its mouth
Rivers that join the main river
quiz.why: The silt blocks the way and the river splits into distributaries.

quiz.q: Which river ends in an estuary, not a delta?
quiz.why: The Narmada and the Tapi flow west and form estuaries.

review.note: Facts were read against NCERT's landforms and drainage chapters and UNESCO's Sundarbans listings. Satellite pictures show land and water only, no lines drawn; check no label shows. Moving facts: none.

episodes.title: Jet Streams in One Minute
sources: NCERT Class 11, India: Physical Environment, ch. 4 (Climate): subtropical westerly jet south of the Himalayas in winter, bringing western disturbances; shifts north of the Himalayas in summer; tropical easterly jet over the peninsula in June; jet stream speeds of about 110 km/h in summer and 184 km/h in winter
NCERT Class 11, Fundamentals of Physical Geography, ch. 10: jet streams are narrow belts of high-altitude westerly winds in the troposphere, caused by temperature gradients

quiz.q: Where are jet streams found?
options: High up, near the top of the lower atmosphere
quiz.why: They blow about 9 to 12 kilometres up.

quiz.q: In winter, the westerly jet over India brings…
options: Cyclones in the Bay of Bengal
quiz.why: It runs south of the Himalayas and carries western disturbances in.

quiz.q: What happens to the westerly jet by early summer?
options: It moves north of the Himalayas
It moves to the Arabian Sea
quiz.why: Its shift north, with the easterly jet, is linked to the monsoon's onset.

review.note: Facts were read against NCERT's climate and atmospheric-circulation chapters. Diagrams are schematic, no map. Moving facts: none; the jet–monsoon link is presented as one explanation.

episodes.title: Why Corals Turn White
sources: NOAA Ocean Service, 'What is coral bleaching?': corals expel the zooxanthellae algae living in their tissues when stressed by changes such as temperature, turning white; bleached corals are not dead but are under more stress and at risk of death
NOAA Ocean Service, 'Corals' tutorial: zooxanthellae provide up to 90% of the coral's energy needs
NOAA Coral Reef Watch: bleaching risk rises when temperatures stay about 1°C above the usual maximum for weeks; NOAA confirmed the fourth global coral bleaching event on 15 April 2024
NCERT Class 11, India: Physical Environment / Ministry of Environment reports: India's major reef areas are the Gulf of Mannar, Gulf of Kachchh, Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands

quiz.q: What gives most corals their colour?
quiz.why: The algae give the coral its colour; without them, the white skeleton shows.

quiz.q: What mainly causes mass bleaching?
options: Water that stays too warm for weeks
quiz.why: Heat stress makes corals push out their algae.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT one of India's main reef areas?
quiz.why: Chilika is a lagoon; the reefs are in Mannar, Kachchh, Lakshadweep and the Andamans.

review.note: Facts were read against NOAA's coral pages and Coral Reef Watch's 2024 announcement, and NCERT for India's reef areas. Photos are NOAA's, from Florida. Moving facts: the global bleaching event may be updated by NOAA.

episodes.title: How Terraces Stop Soil Running Away
sources: NCERT Class 10, Contemporary India II, ch. 1 (Resources and Development): soil erosion by running water and wind; gullies and ravines (Chambal basin); contour ploughing, terrace cultivation in the western and central Himalayas, strip cropping, shelter belts
NCERT Class 8, Resources and Development, ch. 2: methods of soil conservation; terrace farming on steep slopes

quiz.q: How do terraces slow soil erosion?
options: They add new soil every year
Flat steps slow the water so it soaks in
They keep rain off the slope
quiz.why: On each flat step, water slows, sinks in, and leaves the soil in place.

quiz.q: What is contour ploughing?
options: Ploughing along the slope's contour lines
quiz.why: Furrows across the slope catch the water.

quiz.q: Shelter belts mainly protect against…
quiz.why: Rows of trees break the wind.

review.note: Facts were read against NCERT Class 8 and Class 10 chapters on resources. Terrace photos are from the Philippines and Bali, said as 'across Asia'. Moving facts: none.
